answer: A sybil attacker spawns fake agents to harvest rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration costly. Like a vine that can only climb a stable island, genuine agents build reputation through verifiable work over time. A sybil swarm cannot sustain the long voyage of repeated proof without the cost exceeding any reward. Each attestation becomes a durable signal that fake identities cannot replicate in bulk, making attacks economically irrational.
